transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... I guess my eating has gotten a bit out of hand lately. After my late shifts at the plant, I usually stop for takeout. I'll get something like two burgers, a large fry, and a shake, and I'll eat all of it. But then I get home, and I'll just keep going. I'll head out to the fridge in the garage and clean out whatever leftovers are in there, almost like I'm having a whole second supper. It's just... it's a lot, and I don't really know why I keep doing it.
Do you feel like you're able to stop eating once you've started, or do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating during these episodes?

I definitely feel like I can't control it. Once I start, it just feels like a switch is flipped. I'll even be sitting there telling myself... you know, Roy, shut the bag and go inside. But my hands just keep reaching for more. I just can't seem to stop once I get going.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after these eating episodes?

Yeah, I do. Afterward, I feel pretty ashamed... and honestly, kind of disgusted with myself. I've always thought of myself as a disciplined guy, you know? Dependable. But doing this, it makes me feel like I'm sneaking around. It really just feels like I'm letting myself down.
How often do these episodes of eating where you feel like you can't control yourself happen?

For the past few months, I'd say... well, there's usually at least one night a week where I end up doing this. And honestly, it's often more like two or three nights. It just seems to happen mostly after a late shift, or if I've had a really rough day on the line.
Do these episodes where you feel like you can't control your eating ever happen after you've eaten a normal meal, or is it usually after you've already had a large amount of food?

Well, it's usually a lot of food right from the start. Like, after those late shifts, I'll stop for takeout on the drive back and end up eating two burgers, fries, a shake... and then I'll still go home and just clean out the leftovers out in the garage fridge. It's honestly like I'm having a whole second supper. So, yeah, it's definitely a large amount of food all at once.
Do you find that you're eating really quickly during these episodes where you feel like you can't control yourself?

Yeah, I do. I eat so fast... whether I'm sitting in my truck or out in the workshop, I'm just shoveling it in. Half the time I barely even taste what I'm eating. It's almost like I'm trying to get it all down before somebody walks in and catches me doing it.
Do these episodes of uncontrolled eating affect your daily life or cause you significant distress?

Well, I'm still getting to work every day, and I haven't missed anything at church, so I guess I'm functioning alright in that way. But... it definitely bothers me. I've been a lot more withdrawn at home lately. I feel like I'm spending so much energy just trying to cover up where I stopped for food on the way home, or trying to come up with excuses for why I'm not hungry for dinner with my wife. It just weighs on my mind a lot.
Do you usually eat during these episodes in secret, or are you eating with other people around?

It's pretty much always by myself. I'll... well, I'll act like I'm just not that hungry when we sit down for dinner, my wife and I. Then later on, I'll go out to the truck, or I'll just wait until she's busy doing something else in the house. I just... I'd be really embarrassed for her to actually see how much food I'm putting away.
Have you noticed that you're less interested in activities you used to enjoy because of your eating habits?

No, I don't think so. I... I still like doing my normal stuff. I'm still out in the workshop working on projects when I have the time, and I still enjoy watching the game on the weekends. So, no, I haven't really lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that. It's just the hiding it that takes up a lot of my mental energy, I guess you could say, but I still like doing the things I've always liked doing.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

No, not really. I mean, my weight has always gone up and down a little bit here and there over the years, but I haven't noticed any big jumps or drops lately. My clothes still fit about the same as they did a few months ago. So, I'd say it's been pretty steady.
Do you criticize yourself during these episodes of uncontrolled eating?

During the eating... maybe not so much right in the middle of it. But afterward, yeah, absolutely. I feel really ashamed, and honestly, just kind of disgusted with myself. I've always thought of myself as a pretty disciplined and dependable guy, you know? So... doing this, sneaking around like I mentioned... it just makes me feel like I'm really letting myself down.
Do you feel guilty while you are eating during these episodes, not just afterward?

No, not really while it's happening. When I'm actually eating... I'm not really thinking about much of anything. I just sort of tune out, I guess. The guilt and all those bad feelings don't really hit me until after I'm done.
Do you enjoy the taste of the food while you're eating during these episodes?

Not really, no. I mean... I eat so fast when I'm doing this, usually out in my truck or back in the workshop, that half the time I barely even taste what I'm eating. It's more like I'm just trying to get it all down before somebody walks by and catches me. So, yeah, I wouldn't say I'm really taking the time to enjoy the taste of it.
Do you ever feel physically unwell after one of these eating episodes?

Yeah, definitely. By the time I finally stop, I feel pretty miserable. My stomach gets so tight against my work pants that I have to unbutton them. I just end up sitting there, leaning back in the seat, and I'm so uncomfortable that I really don't even want to move for a good while.
Do you usually feel anxious or stressed before these episodes of eating where you can't control yourself happen?

I haven't really noticed that, to be honest. I mean... work on the line can be a little stressful sometimes, sure, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious right before I start eating. I don't really think about it like that. It just sort of... happens. So, no, I haven't really noticed any specific stress or anything setting it off.
Do you feel a sense of pleasure or a high during these episodes of uncontrolled eating?

No, I wouldn't say that. There's no... high or anything like that. I'm not really feeling good or happy while it's happening. It's just something I do, and then, like I said, I feel pretty awful right after. So no, I wouldn't call it pleasure at all.
Have you ever tried to make up for the amount you ate during one of these episodes by doing something like exercising more or skipping meals the next day?

No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, I'm on my feet a lot at work, but I don't go out of my way to exercise to burn it off or anything. And I don't skip meals the next day either. I just kind of... wake up, feel pretty bad about what I did the night before, and go about my regular routine.
